findings.description: Preserve completed results independently of post-result worker success. The status==0 requirement discards a fully delivered publication marker when after() fails or times out. Guardian then fixes barrier=False and retains fences indefinitely instead of reaching its persisted-byte comparison. Both failures represent this single compatibility/liveness regression.
findings.evidence: Fresh joined run: 51 passed, 17 subtests passed, 2 failed. Additional unchanged probes confirm both implementations reap their children and return exit codes -9/71; baseline retains the completed marker, candidate returns None. Guardian lines 325-338 intentionally derives barrier from the marker without requiring status 0, then verifies actual persisted bytes under fences. owner-window.py:91 supplies no hook; guardian defaults hook=None, so normal CLI supplies no after callback. All four read consumers require status 0 and a non-None result. These callback failures do not demonstrate a normal successful CLI blocker; abnormal termination after delivery can still leave custody unresolved.
findings.fix: Separate complete-result evidence from worker success inside native_job. Positively identify full bounded-result completion before after(), preserve/drain completed evidence after failure or timeout, and return it with the actual wait status only after positive reaping. Keep partial, malformed and oversized results unusable; accepting a syntactically valid prefix is insufficient. Preserve identity gating, deadlines, reaping, retained fences and guardian persisted-byte verification. Align README semantics and independently re-review the correction without suppressing or changing the independent oracle.
